overview: Bailiffs keep order and safety in courtrooms. They screen people entering the courthouse, escort prisoners, guard juries and enforce the judge's rules during trials. O*NET rates their knowledge of public safety at 4.26 out of 5 and law and government at 4.09. Many bailiffs start with a high school diploma (40%) or an associate degree (33%), plus police or corrections training. The BLS May 2025 median is $56,600 across 17,310 jobs. Hours are usually regular, often within 40 a week, and the work follows clear procedures with frequent contact with the public.
pay: Bailiff pay varies more by state than most jobs. The national median is $56,600, but Connecticut's state median is $111,890, 98% above it, and Alaska pays $90,600. New York has the most bailiffs, 3,830, with a median of $77,540. North Dakota has the lowest state median, $27,560.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $56,600 a year. The lowest 10% earn under $32,140 and the top 10% earn $96,770 or more. Connecticut, Alaska and Massachusetts have the highest state medians, while Kentucky ($30,760) and North Dakota ($27,560) pay the least.

faq.q: How do you become a bailiff?
faq.a: Most courts hire through the sheriff's office or state court system. In O*NET data, 40% of bailiffs have a high school diploma, 21% a post-secondary certificate and 33% an associate degree. Many complete law enforcement or corrections training, and a background check is standard.

faq.q: What does a bailiff do every day?
faq.a: A bailiff screens visitors with metal detectors, escorts people in custody, calls cases and keeps the courtroom orderly. O*NET rates monitoring and speaking at 3.38 out of 5 for this job. Self-control and integrity stand out as work styles, since you stay calm in tense hearings.

faq.q: What careers can bailiffs move into?
faq.a: The closest moves are supervisors of correctional officers (88% match) and police and detective supervisors (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Police supervisors earn $106,040, 87% more than bailiffs, according to BLS May 2025, though most need police academy training and experience first.
